summary.en: Use the **future continuous** for an action in progress at a future moment: _This time tomorrow I'll be flying to Lima._ Use the **future perfect** for an action that will be finished **by** a future moment: _By Friday I'll have finished the report._ The future continuous is also a polite way to ask about plans: _Will you be using the car tonight?_
summary.es: Future continuous: estaré haciendo algo en ese momento. Future perfect: para entonces ya habré terminado. Fíjate en by (para entonces, a más tardar) frente a at / this time (en ese momento).

form: Time words: _this time next week_, _at 8 tomorrow_ (continuous); _by Friday_, _by the time_, _by then_ (perfect)
After _by the time_, _when_ and _before_ use the present simple, not will

uses.text: **In progress at a future moment** → _At noon tomorrow I'**ll be sitting** my driving test._
**Finished before a future moment** → _By next June she'**ll have graduated**._
**Polite questions about plans** → _**Will** you **be passing** the post office later?_

note.en: It sounds less direct than asking "Are you going to…?" because it does not ask for a favour outright.
note.es: Suena menos directo que pedir el favor abiertamente.

uses.text: **Things that will happen anyway** → _I'**ll be seeing** Maria at the meeting, so I'll ask her._
**Predicting duration** → _In September they'**ll have been** married for ten years._

mistakes.wrong: By Friday I'll be finishing the report.
mistakes.right: By Friday I'll have finished the report.

why.en: By + a time means finished before that time, so use the future perfect.
why.es: By + momento = terminado antes de ese momento: future perfect.

mistakes.wrong: By the time you will arrive, we'll have left.
mistakes.right: By the time you arrive, we'll have left.

why.en: After by the time, use the present simple for the future.
why.es: Tras by the time: presente simple, no will.

mistakes.wrong: Tomorrow at six I'll work in the garden.
mistakes.right: Tomorrow at six I'll be working in the garden.

why.en: An action in progress at a future moment takes the future continuous.
why.es: Acción en curso en un momento futuro: future continuous.

examples.en: This time next week, I'll be lying on a beach in Crete.
examples.es: A esta hora la semana que viene estaré tumbado en una playa de Creta.

examples.en: By the end of the month, we'll have saved enough for a deposit.
examples.es: A finales de mes habremos ahorrado lo suficiente para la entrada.

examples.en: Don't call at eight. We'll be having dinner.
Will you be needing the projector this afternoon?
By 2030, the company will have opened offices in six countries.
I won't have finished the course by the time you leave.
Will she have heard the news by now?
In ten years, many of us will be working from home.
When you wake up, I'll already have left for the airport.

practice.prompt: Don't phone me at nine tomorrow. I ___ in an interview.

explanation.en: An action in progress at a future moment: future continuous.

practice.prompt: By the time you get here, we ___ all the food.

explanation.en: By the time shows completion before then: future perfect.

practice.prompt: ___ the car this evening, or can I borrow it?

explanation.en: A polite question about your plans: future continuous.

practice.prompt: By next year she ___ here for a decade.

explanation.en: A total period completed by a future point: future perfect.
